templates.name: Linux Tools (Example Music)
templates.description:
Companion template for ansible/playbooks/linux/tools.yml -- the first of Robert's 'every playbook gets a Zabbix template' initiative (2026-10-16).

HOW IT WORKS
  One master item reads /etc/example-music/zabbix_status/linux_tools.json via vfs.file.contents every hour -- currently just update_motd_linked, written by linux/tools.yml itself at the end of every run. That file also drives the staleness trigger below. Package presence is a SEPARATE mechanism, see PACKAGE DISCOVERY.

PACKAGE DISCOVERY (one item per package, not an aggregate)
  A discovery rule reads /etc/example-music/zabbix_status/linux_tools_packages_lld.json, also written by linux/tools.yml -- an LLD-format {"data":[{"{#PACKAGE}":"..."}]} list of every package in common_packages (group_vars/all/main.yml). Ansible owns WHICH packages are in scope (it's the only source of truth for common_packages); it deliberately does NOT re-report whether each one is installed -- that's a genuinely native, independent agent-side check per discovered package: vfs.file.exists[/usr/share/doc/{#PACKAGE}/copyright]. Debian policy requires every binary package to ship a copyright file at that path (real file or a symlink when sharing docs with another binary from the same source) -- a stable, checksum-independent proxy for 'is this package installed', with no custom UserParameter script needed. One item + one trigger per discovered package, not a single missing_packages_count/list pair -- that was v1's mistake, corrected same day once Robert flagged it ('this crap... one package per item').
  Known limitation: a package whose doc directory was deleted by something outside dpkg (rare, broken state) would false-negative here even though dpkg still lists it installed -- accepted, not solved, since classic zabbix-agent has no native dpkg-aware key and this avoids deploying a custom script just to cover that edge case.

STALENESS
  The {$LINUXTOOLS.STATUS.MAXAGE} macro (default 2d) drives a nodata() trigger on the master item itself -- catches linux/tools.yml not having run recently at all, not just config drift the report would otherwise go stale on.

IMPORT INSTRUCTIONS
  Zabbix API: configuration.import (rules: createMissing for groups/templates/items/triggers/discoveryRules, updateExisting for the rest). Or via the UI: Data collection -> Templates -> Import.
  Link to each Linux host this playbook manages.

items.name: Linux Tools: status report (master)
items.description: Raw JSON status report written by linux/tools.yml at the end of every run. All other items in this template depend on this one.

triggers.name: Linux Tools: no status report for {$LINUXTOOLS.STATUS.MAXAGE} on {HOST.NAME} -- linux/tools.yml may not be running
triggers.description: linux/tools.yml hasn't written a fresh status report within {$LINUXTOOLS.STATUS.MAXAGE}. Either the playbook hasn't run against this host recently, or the zabbix-agent/file path is broken. Check: ls -la /etc/example-music/zabbix_status/linux_tools.json and re-run linux/tools.yml.

items.name: Linux Tools: update-motd symlink healthy
items.description: 1 if /etc/update-motd.d/98-update-status is a real symlink to /usr/local/bin/update-motd, 0 otherwise.

triggers.name: Linux Tools: update-motd not linked on {HOST.NAME}
triggers.description: The update-motd symlink is missing or broken. Re-run linux/tools.yml -- see its 'Link update-motd into /etc/update-motd.d' task.

discovery_rules.name: Linux Tools: package discovery
discovery_rules.description: Reads the LLD-format package list written by linux/tools.yml (one {#PACKAGE} entry per common_packages name, group_vars/all/main.yml). lifetime=7d: a package dropped from common_packages has its item/trigger cleaned up within a week rather than lingering forever.

item_prototypes.name: Package installed: {#PACKAGE}
item_prototypes.description: 1 if /usr/share/doc/{#PACKAGE}/copyright exists (real file or symlink -- Debian policy requires every binary package to ship one), 0 otherwise. Native agent check, independent of linux/tools.yml's own ansible_facts.packages -- Ansible only supplies the list of packages to watch, not whether each is installed.

triggers.name: Linux Tools: package {#PACKAGE} missing on {HOST.NAME}
triggers.description: {#PACKAGE} is in common_packages (group_vars/all/main.yml) but /usr/share/doc/{#PACKAGE}/copyright doesn't exist -- package is not installed, or was removed outside Ansible. Re-run linux/tools.yml.

macros.description: How long the status report can go without a fresh write before the staleness trigger fires. Override per-host if a host is deliberately on a less frequent Ansible run schedule.
